title: The Invention of Love by Tom Stoppard at Theaterlab #theinventionoflo...
transcript: I feel like Tom Stoppard's plays are often better read and studied than actually experienced live. This production didn't necessarily change my mind, but oh, what a treat it is to see David Greenspan in anything ever. The Invention of Love is about scholar and poet A.E. Housman at the end of his life on his journey to the underworld. It starts as somewhat of a memory play, morphs into a straight up philosophy lecture, and then back into a drama. Housman reminisces on his time at Oxford where he studied literature, and the unrequited love he had for a friend that captured him and never let him go. Of the almost three hour run time though, I wouldn't say the majority of it is spent on the primary story — hence the philosophy lecture. Many plays sprinkle their wisdom and philosophical nuggets throughout, but this one plasters them all over. Everything from education, art, truth, criticism, even electricity are on the table here. Much of this material is delivered by Housman himself, and David Greenspan's regal presence enables him to convey this hybrid of dialogue, lecture and poetry with a gentleness but an assuredness nonetheless. Although he was the main draw here for me, I was glad to see this rarely produced play, though I can see why it's rarely produced. There’s a lot to take away from this compelling piece, but whether it's compelling as a play is more of a debate. With that, another program for My collection.
